rv.q: Broadway has had two big disappointing attempts at this mother of all alienation dramas in recent memory -- once with Sting in 1989, the other with Alan Cumming in 2006.
This Threepenny Opera has many virtues, but it lacks the acrid bite and political urgency that should make Brecht's 1928 musical feel vital and dangerous.
This is one party where the hangover begins almost as soon as the evening does.
Clarke's vision of the dark and moody Kurt Weill-Bertolt Brecht opera, fails to come together in a compelling or cohesive way.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actor in a Musical

cn.t: Critics are divided on this production, with some praising Clarke's intimate vision for capturing corruption's pleasures without excess, while others find it anemic and lacking Brecht's vital political bite.

vs.sum: An intimate 299-seat black box space at Roundabout, offering an unusually close actor-audience experience unlike any other Broadway house. Sightlines and sound vary by configuration since staging changes per production. Comfort is adequate but unremarkable.

acc.note: Accessible by elevator only. Assistive listening devices available.
